geometryObservations: No bottomless pits on the jungle path: every gap is lava on part of the path (G-S1-a, G-S1-b, G-S2-a, G-S2-b, G-S3-a) or, only in the chase, a full band (G-S4-a, G-S4-b). The path stays continuous, so lava acts as lane denial and death comes from being pushed or hurried into it.

Enemy and lava are paired on purpose: Crafish stand beside lava patches and their counter-hit throws Crash far (F3 p032R); POINT 1 teaches waiting next to lava in S1, and POINT A on the yellow course spells out that a wrong spin ends in the fire (E-S1-a → E-YELLOW-b).

Timed vents (geysers) sit on the dry lane next to the lava (O-S1-b), so the safe lane is also the timed lane; the Baby T's high jump is designed for exactly that stretch, and its ride ends where the hazard mix changes (P-S2-a, P3 shot 4).

Clinging grass is a speed gate whose cost depends on context: free in S1 (O-S1-a), unavoidable between Nitros on the yellow course (O-YELLOW-b), and deadly in the chase (O-S4-b) — one surface, three difficulty levels.

Ambushers guard checkpoints: wave researchers rise from holes just before C1, before C2, after C2 and beside the yellow checkpoint (E-S1-c, E-S2-b, E-S3-a, E-YELLOW-c), punishing a sprint to the save.

Explosive stacks are placed on the narrowest footing (the sand strip above lava, P-YELLOW-b): the super body slam's reach and the retreat distance from the TNT become part of the geometry (POINT B: slam from a distance, step away).

The side-view lava area replaces horizontal gaps with vertical ones: a crate staircase (P-S3-c), an arrow column that is eaten bounce by bounce (G-S3-b), and a switch-built steel bar over a mine pair (P-S3-d).

The chase is run toward the camera, so obstacles appear late; it uses short, readable hazards (lava bands, a geyser, grass, two fliers) and saves the only moving gap — the spreading lava band — for the end (O-S4-c).

The pursuer is telegraphed: the triceratops waits in a gully before C3 (E-S4-a), the save sits between the reveal and the chase, and the chaser breaks every crate left behind, so the chase tests movement and never the box count.

Pterodactyls carry two roles: a secret exit when they pick you up on the yellow course (E-YELLOW-d) and a side hazard in the chase (E-S4-b/c); the same touch rule reads as reward or punishment depending on placement.
Rest spaces are clearings with big crate structures (the 3×3 wall clearing, the lava-area pyramid); the narrow corridors between them carry the lava, enemies and grass.
The bonus uses thin slabs with 1–2 u gaps purely as slam stations, and ends with the slam's reach over a gap (G-BONUS-b): the geometry exists to demonstrate the move's radius.
geometryTransfer: Lava as lane denial: on a 4–5 m path, `pit` patches (lava look) 2–3 m long covering half the width, alternating sides every 6–10 m; skaters weave at cruise, walkers keep to the dry half. Put a `spinner` beside each patch so a careless spin or knock-back leads into it.

Clinging grass with `groundSpeedLimit` (≈2.4 m/s) patches across the path: harmless early, flanked by Nitros later so it cannot be bypassed, and inside a pursuit last; a full jump (≈5.6 m) clears a 2.3–3.5 m patch and gives the speed-keeping answer.

Geyser stand-in: no vent primitive exists, so use a short-cycle `crusher` or `firetiki` placed on the dry lane next to a lava patch, and give a rideable/ally section (or the skateboard) the jump that clears it.

Chase toward the camera: a `zone` with dir N and a `stone` pursuer; lava `pit` bands 2–2.5 m every 12–18 m (inside the 5.6 m running jump), one grass patch, and crates kept off the racing line (on the board they trip the rider below 12.5 m/s); end with the widest band.

Side-view ledge above lava: `zone` E over a `pit`, a 2.3 m-deep earth ledge, a crate pyramid as stairs, a steel arrow under three floating crates with a `bang` on top that materialises a steel ledge over two Nitros (arrow 3.77 m, held 5.92 m above its lid).

Explosive stack on narrow footing: a 3 m strip with an iron/TNT stack; our slam radius is 3.4 m and the blast 2.75 m, so leave at least 4 m of strip behind the slam point for the retreat, and never put the stack on the only lane of a board line.
